_about: ParaTrooper, Orion Software, 1982. A .COM whose first seven bytes are
a far jump: the game proper starts at file 0x2B40 with DS = PSP + 0x11,
so every address below is its file offset minus 0x10.
All 19 call targets are named, and so is every routine the four-entry
phase table jumps to. The globals were read from what touches them,
and then checked against bss_clear_table at 0x1A30 -- the program's own
list of its variables. All 17 entries land on a name here with the
Three names in the previous version of this file were wrong, and all
three had been guessed from caller counts: draw_sprite is the random
number generator, move_actor is the sound queue, spawn is a blitter.

0x2B40: the far jump at file 0 lands here with DS = PSP + 0x11, which is why every data address in this listing is its file offset minus 0x10. Checks the BIOS equipment word for a colour adapter, sets mode 4, animates the eleven title letters, plays the 123-note tune, and waits for space or the joystick button
0x2DB0: the round loop for waves 0 and 1. Draws the ground line at 0x1DB0 and the gun base, prints the status line, then paces itself on INT 1Ah ticks: move the helicopter lanes, move the falling troopers, step the bullets, redraw the gun
0x3152: phase 1 of the wave table: clear the spawn flags and fall back into the helicopter loop
0x315F: phase 2: refuses to start while a trooper is still climbing, then points the sprite pointers at the jets (0xB8E/0xA9E) and enters the bomber loop
0x3195: writes a zero divisor to PIT channel 2 and returns from the round -- the one exit the game has
0x319E: phase 3: stop spawning and keep the bombers flying
0x31A6: phase 0: pick a direction from the RNG, bump the wave counter at 0x1AB5, and scale the difficulty from it -- bomb allowance up to ten, lane geometry from wave*6 until wave 17
0x3223: forces phase 2 and starts the alarm tone; the only writer of 0x1AE3
0x3235: state = state * 0x7781 + 0x64C9. A linear congruential generator, seeded from the INT 1Ah tick count at start-up. It was called draw_sprite because seven routines call it
0x3244: a falling trooper reached the stack top for its column. Picks the counter by column -- under 0x43 left, under 0x53 the gun base, otherwise right -- increments it, scores five, raises column_stack_top by 0x140, and draws the standing figure. Four at the gun base jumps straight to explode_gun
0x3360: the round loop for waves 2 and 3: the same shape as play_helicopters, but the aircraft drop bombs instead of troopers and a bomb that reaches the ground ends the game
0x365C: steps thirty bullets. Each is erased with INT 10h AH=0Ch colour 0, advanced by the (dx, dy) pair its angle selects from bullet_velocity, redrawn in colour 3, and tested for a hit. Then reads the keyboard, or the joystick if joystick_mode is set. It was called video_setup because it was the only routine holding both INT 10h and INT 16h
0x36FF: stops the gun rotating, queues the firing tone, takes one point off the score, and claims the first free bullet slot -- the 'each bullet you fire costs you one point' the instructions screen promises
0x3733: the arrow-key and auto-repeat path: steps gun_angle by two within [0, max_gun_angle]
0x3752: the end of the game. Sets phase 4 for a hundred ticks, then reads the current gun sprite through gun_angle and scatters all 168 of its bytes into the particle array as individual flying pixels
0x3830: stores AL into climb_dir and clears climb_active
0x3839: the human ladder. Once four troopers are stacked on one side they walk toward the gun: find the shortest neighbouring stack, step onto it, and redraw. Reaching the gun base tail-calls explode_gun
0x3944: eight rows of one byte from climber_sprite_b, bank-interleaved
0x3965: the same eight rows written as zero
0x397E: picks climber_sprite_a or climber_sprite_c by the low bit of the screen offset -- the two-pixel phase of a four-pixel column
0x39B0: decrements the eight sound timers; the first one still running dispatches through sound_handler. Silent while sound_enabled is negative. It was called move_actor
0x39F1: writes divisor 2 then AH to PIT channel 2 -- the tail every sound handler falls into
0x3A6A: ten rows of BP bytes from SI, advancing the source by six a row so a six-byte aircraft sprite can be drawn narrower at the screen edges. It was called spawn
0x3A8E: what a bullet ran into. Aircraft first (both lanes, six cells either side, ten points), then bombs if the phase is 2 to 4 (thirty points), then parachutes and falling troopers (five). Every hit shatters the sprite it hit into the particle array
0x3DFE: moves the three hundred live particles: erase, add velocity, add 0x8028 of gravity, kill any that leave the 0x19F0/0x39F0 window, redraw
0x3E68: adds AL to the six-digit score, one decimal digit per byte, then falls into score_draw
0x3E8C: renders the six digits right to left from digit_font, sixteen bytes a glyph, suppressing leading zeros by substituting the eleventh glyph
0x3EDE: the same borrow-propagating subtraction of one, and it returns early rather than wrap a score of zero
0x3F12: ten countdown timers; when one reaches zero the standing trooper whose screen offset sits at +0x14 is erased
0x3F41: the analogue path: port 0x201 for the two buttons, then the capacitor-discharge loop counted into CX and divided by seven for the gun angle. Also honours Ctrl-S and Escape

0x0000: 21 words, stride 0x68: the gun at 21 angles
0x08BA: set by the wave handlers to 0x9AE or 0xB8E
0x08BC: 0x8BE or 0xA9E; the pair is read as [di + 0x8BB] with di = +/-1
0x0C7E: 22 rows of 3 bytes; its last 8 rows are the body sprite
0x0CA8: 8 rows of 3 -- the same bytes as the tail of the parachute
0x0CF5: 256 bytes, each 0x59 past the last -- how a particle picks its velocity
0x0DF5: 0x0270, 0x0276, 0x027C ... the RNG cut-offs for opening a parachute
0x0F85: 123 PIT divisors, one per timer tick
0x1167: 11 pointers at +2..+0x16 into 6 distinct bitmaps -- PARATROOPER has six distinct letters
0x117F: 6 x 24 rows x 5 bytes, ending exactly where digit_font begins
0x144F: 11 glyphs of 16 bytes: 7 rows of 2, plus a blank at index 10 for leading zeros
0x14FF: 6 (cursor position, string) pairs -- the author, the copyright, the two ways to play
0x159C: 3 more of the same, shown after a round
0x1606: the *Your Mission* screen; bytes under 4 are colour changes, 0 ends it
0x1962: printed if the player answers N to the adapter question, then the program hangs
0x19F6: 'Do you have the Color/Graphics Monitor Adapter(Y/N)?'
0x1A30: 17 (address, length) pairs -- the game's own account of its variables, and the cross-check for this file
0x1A74: 'SCORE:' then 18 blanks then 'HI-SCORE:' -- 39 characters printed once per round
0x1A7A: where score_draw's digits land inside status_line
0x1A95: and where the high score's do
0x1A9B: 6 digits, one per byte, compared against score with a reverse repe cmpsb
0x1AB0: the INT 1Ah reading the frame loop spins against
0x1AB3: counts down; zero advances the phase
0x1AB5: how many waves have started; the only difficulty input
0x1AD7: 0, 60, 120, 180 -- the four animation frames of an aircraft, 60 bytes apart
0x1ADB: seeded from the tick count at start-up
0x1AE3: set by enter_bomber_phase and read nowhere else in the code region
0x1AE7: 100 bytes, one per column: which aircraft occupies it
0x1BAF: one word per column: the falling trooper's screen offset, sign = parachute open
0x1C4F: the parallel array bullet_hit_test reads as [si - 0xA2]
0x1D8F: the loop variable stepping 2, 0 over the two lanes
0x1DA7: {0x50, -4} -- which end of the lane the walk starts from
0x1DAC: cleared while a climber is on the stack
0x1DAD: set when a landing made four on one side
0x1DAE: 78 words, all 0x1DB0 at the start -- the ground line. Each landed trooper raises its column by 0x140, which is eight scan lines across the two banks
0x1E4A: the 78 words copied over it at the start of a game
0x1EE6: non-zero while any aircraft is still in a lane
0x1EF2: 10 words; zero means the slot is free
0x1F1A: at +0x28, gaining 0x8028 of gravity every fourth tick
0x1F56: chosen at the title screen and never changed
0x1F57: 0 to 40 in twos; also the index into gun_sprite_table, which is why the draw reads [[gun_angle]]
0x1F59: 30 words; zero means the slot is free
0x1FD1: at +0x78; the gun angle the shot was fired at
0x200D: 21 (dx, dy) pairs, indexed by angle x 2
0x2065: non-zero repeats the last arrow key; firing clears it
0x2066: 16 words, picked by the low five bits of the RNG
0x2086: 104 bytes; explode_gun shatters this copy, not the original
0x2131: the eight columns of the gun base; four here ends the game
0x2134: written by climber_step; read by climber_step; holds 1
0x2135: where the climbing figure is drawn
0x2137: written by climber_step; read by climber_step
0x2139: alternates the two halves of a step
0x213A: reloaded with 3 -- a climber moves every third tick
0x2153: 8 countdowns; slot 1 is the bomb, 2 the hit, 3 the shot, 4 the explosion
0x215B: 8 code addresses, all ending in speaker_off
0x216B: negated by Ctrl-S, in four different places
0x216C: 600 bytes; the byte value each flying pixel carries
0x2AEC: the bullet bullet_hit_test is working on
0x2AEE: walks shuffle_table so consecutive particles fly differently
0x2AF0: written by bullet_hit_test and explode_gun; read by bullet_hit_test and explode_gun; holds 0x24
0x2AF1: the bullet's x, divided by four and shifted five left
0x2AF3: written by bullet_hit_test; read by bullet_hit_test
0x2AF5: written by bullet_hit_test; read by bullet_hit_test
0x2AF7: walks the sprite being shattered, one byte a step
0x2AF9: alternates +0x1FFA and its complement -- the CGA bank interleave
0x2AFB: -1, 0 or +1 by which third of the screen the hit was in
0x2B00: 6 digits, one per byte, least significant first
0x2B2E: reloaded with 3 while the joystick button is held
0x1D99: the second entry of lane_screen; the wave handlers set it directly
0x1DA1: the second entry of flight_dir, set to +1 for the bomber lane
0x2154: sound_timers[1] -- 0x32 when a bomb is released, 0 when it is destroyed
0x2155: sound_timers[2] -- 0x14, set by every scoring hit
0x2157: sound_timers[4] -- 0x61, the longest, set by explode_gun
es:0x0010: 0040:0010. start reads bits 0x30 to find the adapter and writes 0x20 back to claim 40-column colour
0x08BB: the midpoint of aircraft_sprite_left and aircraft_sprite_right; the lane code reads [di + 0x8BB] with di = +/-1 to pick a side
0x10A1: read as [bx + 0x10A1] while the title letters are drawn
0x1163: title_letter_table reached with the loop's own base; the first entry used is +2
0x1BF2: fall_offset with the column already biased by 0x43 -- the same array the bomb spawn walks
0x1DA4: edge_step reached with the direction in DI, so the base is one entry below
0x200F: bullet_velocity + 2: the dy of each (dx, dy) pair
0x2062: max_gun_angle reached with the index already in SI
0x2159: sound_handler less the two the index starts at
0x04AE: the +0x4AE displacement from a particle's pixel byte to its speed
0x04AF: the same as a word write
ds:0x1167: 11 pointers at +2..+0x16 into 6 distinct bitmaps -- PARATROOPER has six distinct letters; also written [ds:...] in 1 place, which is the same address -- the prefix only overrides the default segment for the base register
ds:0x2066: 16 words, picked by the low five bits of the RNG; also written [ds:...] in 1 place, which is the same address -- the prefix only overrides the default segment for the base register
ds:0x1D99: the second entry of lane_screen; the wave handlers set it directly; also written [ds:...] in 1 place, which is the same address -- the prefix only overrides the default segment for the base register
ds:0x1D91: +1 or -1, copied out of flight_dir; also written [ds:...] in 2 places, which is the same address -- the prefix only overrides the default segment for the base register
ds:0x1D95: the second entry of lane_cells; also written [ds:...] in 1 place, which is the same address -- the prefix only overrides the default segment for the base register
ds:0x1D9D: the second lane's, capped at 0x6C; also written [ds:...] in 2 places, which is the same address -- the prefix only overrides the default segment for the base register

_note: The data region is file 0x0000..0x2B40, which is 67% of the image.
Counting named addresses says nothing about the bytes between them,
so these are the spans, and they are contiguous: every byte of the
region belongs to exactly one of them.
0x0000: the gun at 21 angles, table then bitmaps
0x08BA: the two sprite pointers the wave handlers swap
0x08BE: four aircraft sprite sets, 4 variants x 10 rows x 6 bytes each
0x0C7E: the parachute, the falling body, the standing trooper, the bomb
0x0DF5: the parachute thresholds and the space between them and the tune
0x1167: the title letters and the table that orders them
0x14FF: every string in the game, including the whole instructions screen
0x1A30: the bss clear table, the status line, the high score
0x1AB0: the phase machine and the RNG
0x1AE7: the two flight lanes and the three per-column falling arrays
0x1D8F: the lane geometry, two entries wide
0x1DAE: the column stack tops and the copy they are restored from
0x1F59: the bullet arrays and the per-angle velocity table
0x2063: the gun's angle, its scratch copy, and the particle spread
0x2130: the landing counters and the climbing figure
0x216C: 600 particle slots, four arrays of 600 bytes
0x2ACC: the shatter scratch, the score, the landed-trooper timers

_note: 10 bracketed constants in the listing are displacements, not
addresses: each appears only with a base register and never on its own,
and every one is under 0x400 -- a field inside a record the base points
at. They are listed so the coverage number has a denominator that means
something, and so the next reader does not go looking for a variable.
